tweets.text:
A few weeks ago, when everything was pumping and people were constantly pressuring me, I kept getting the same question:

"What's your price invalidation?"

Here's what most people don't understand.

I don't have a price invalidation. I have a STRUCTURAL invalidation.

And yes, I know exactly what would invalidate my thesis.

But none of those conditions have been met.

I'm perfectly willing to change my perspective when the market confirms I'm wrong. I have absolutely no problem with that.

For now, I'll continue focusing on the scenarios I believe have the highest probability of playing out.

I don't have a crystal ball. Nobody does.

But I know how to read market structure, identify probabilities, and anticipate what could come next.

That's what I've been doing all along.

Hope you understand.

> Coinbase CVD at -8.9k BTC vs Binance at -3.1k from nov 9-14

The chart looked fantastic (imo), but yes, that's a lot of sell pressure.

Let's see how markets react to this tomorrow

tweets.text:
I believe the next few decades will bring a massive shift in how we value assets.

While everyone is obsessed with AI, technology, and digital assets, I think some of the biggest opportunities will be found in the physical world.

Land. Farmland. Precious metals. Energy. Water. Natural resources.

Things that are finite, essential, and impossible to replicate with a few lines of code.

Technology can scale almost infinitely. Physical resources cannot.

And as AI and automation continue to expand, the demand for energy, infrastructure, and raw materials could become even more important.

The next great wealth transfer might not be about owning the next big technology.

It might be about owning the scarce resources that technology depends on.
